about: A health assistant on a Cascade pod: a chat with a model over a person's records, with every statement checked against the pod before the person sees it. These are the app's Vitest tests (`test/` and `src/`); its three browser tests in `e2e/` run on Playwright against `npm start` and are not on this page.
capabilities: Loading the sample pod the app opens on · loadSample(), SAMPLE
Serving PodApi to the app's pages · appServer(), POST /api/<operation>
Listing what is worth a look in a pod · worthALook()
Saying review reasons, dates and counts in words · reviewSaid(), stepWhenSaid(), dayOrAsWritten()
Tools a model reaches the app by · TOOLS, NEVER
Running the read tools over HTTP · GET /tools, POST /tools/<name>
Making and unlocking pods · api.makePod(), api.unlock()
Titling a pod after a hospital's record is brought in · api.bring()
Asking a model about a pod · GET /chat, POST /chat
Checking a model's reply before a person sees it · POST /chat, data-reply
Asking a model once more for a reply that was not checked · POST /chat, data-checking
Keeping a recommendation in a record's own words · recommendsInOwnVoice(), POST /chat
Saying what a model is doing while it works · workingSaid(), stepSaid(), stepsOf(), Working
Summing up a reply's check in one line · Supporting
Drawing a checked reply as cards · ReplyCards
Bringing a hospital's record into a pod · ConnectionBox
Listing what a model looked at · LookedAt, sideSaid()
build: The sample's downloads, as the evals' case has them

glossary.definition: what a reply says the records lack: the codes and words a record of it would carry (`match`), what was looked through (`coverage`), and the tool call (`query`) or the files (`sources`) that looked.
a part of the app that is there only when its files are. The chat is one: `server/chat.ts`, `models.ts`, `model.ts` and `src/chat/`.
Vercel's `ai` package, through which the server calls a model of any provider and streams the model's turn to the page.
a provider whose models are the Claude family, called through the AI SDK's `@ai-sdk/anthropic`.
of an absence, borne out by what was looked through; an absence that is not comes back with `backed: false` and a `reason`.
`cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }` on a block of a request to Anthropic, which lets the next request read everything up to that block from Anthropic's cache at a lower price.
one item of a checked reply as the chat draws it: the item's sentence, then a chip for each fact and a line for each absence.

what `checkReply` returns for a reply, and the `data` of a `data-reply` part: `errors` when the reply broke the contract; otherwise the `reply`, and for each item its facts, each with whether it passed and what the pod holds of the record (`filled`), and its absences, each with whether it is backed.
one fact of a checked reply as the chat draws it: a rounded label showing what the pod holds of the record, with a check mark when the fact passed.
where a fact points (`cite`): a view entry, a FHIR resource in a download, or a line of one. In a reply about downloads it also gives, field by field, what the fact says the record there holds.
a standard identifier for a kind of thing a record is about, such as a medication or a lab test, that lets records from different sources be matched.
the whole pod as tab-separated text, which the `ask` tool returns a part at a time when called with `format: "compact"`; each line is one row of a view, its cells separated by tabs.

a chunk of the UI message stream that carries the app's own JSON, not the model's text: `data-reply` holds the checked reply, and `data-checking` says the server is asking the model again. A `transient` one is shown and not kept in the chat.
a way a model reaches the app's tools: the chat, or a browser's own model through `document.modelContext`. Every door offers the one list, `TOOLS`.
a file of a person's records as a hospital's server or portal gave it, before any import: FHIR resources in JSON, or a C-CDA document.
a made-up person and their downloads, which cascade-runtime-js's evaluations of models are written against. Priya Natarajan's plants gaps on purpose, among them two downloads an import refuses.
one record an item rests on: what the model says of it, and where it is.
one kind of thing a record says: its `value`, `unit`, `status`, `code`, `name` or `id`, a date (`date`, `start`, `end`, `recorded`), or its text (`text`, from which a `quote` is taken).
why a model stopped, as the AI SDK names it: `stop`, `length` (its output bound ran out), `tool-calls`, `content-filter`, `error` or `other`.
a `<details>` element: one line that a person opens to see what is under it.

a compact read's short name for a view entry: a letter for its view, then the first eight or more hexadecimal digits of the view entry's name, such as `L41e35923`. `ask` takes a list of them in `entries` to return only those view entries' rows.
one point of a reply, with what it rests on.
a story and the exports it uses, which the vocabulary carries for testing, such as `alex-rivera`.
of an item, what the model says from what it knows in general, which no record backs (`knowledge.says`), with the guideline it names for it (`knowledge.guideline`).
a difference between one lab test's results before and after the day a medication started or stopped, as `findChanges()` reports it; it says what moved and never why.
the name a pod gives a record or a view entry to be read by, such as `Allergy entry · Aspirin`, or `Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood` for a lab result.
a language model that an app lets answer a person's questions about their records.
a query the vocabulary carries under a name, such as `pod/My active allergies`.
one function of PodApi, such as `pods`, `answers` or `makePod`.
of a reply, the model speaking for itself, outside the quotation marks round words a record holds.

a tool the page runs itself, because it moves the app (`open_pod`) or writes once the person allows it (`make_pod`). The server offers it to the model and runs nothing, so a call to one ends the server's part of the turn.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
the app's one way to its pods: operations that take JSON and return JSON, which the pages, the tools and the commands all call (`podApi(host)` in `pod-api.ts`).
the made-up person of the evals' case, whose records the sample pod holds.
the company or program that runs a model, such as Anthropic, or a model server on this computer.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
on a call's result, why a rule turned the call down; a refused call wrote nothing.
a model's answer to a person's question about their records, as JSON.
the form a reply must take: an `answer`, a `short` form of it, and `items`. `replySchema` is its JSON Schema, and `replyErrors()` lists where a reply departs from it.
one line of a table: of a view, what one view entry holds, a cell per column; of a reference table, what it says of one code or variant.
here, `cascade-runtime`, the package the app keeps its pods with; it also carries the read tools, the reply contract and `checkReply`, which the app uses as they are.
here, the pod the app opens on: Priya Natarajan's, loaded by `loadSample()` from the sixteen downloads in `samples/priya-natarajan-eval-case/`.
one hospital server, or one document, whose records an export holds.
the words the chat shows under a piece of general knowledge: the guideline the model names for it, or `No source named` when it names none.
here, one tool call of a turn as the chat names it in the app's own words, such as `Read the medications and the day each started`.
a model provider's feature that makes a model reply in a given JSON Schema; providers take only some of JSON Schema's keywords.
what some models write for themselves before a reply. Anthropic counts it against the request's bound on output (`max_tokens`).
a tool's consent: `free` runs at once (it reads, or moves the app), and `ask` runs only after the person allows it (it writes).
here, the unit a model's text is counted and billed in, about four characters of English.
a function a model may call: a name, a description, a JSON Schema for its input, and the code that runs it.
one run of a tool by a model: the tool's name, the input it was given, whether it succeeded, and what it returned.
the app's page that charts one lab test's results over time, around the day a medication started or stopped.
the model's part of a chat after one question: its tool calls, then its reply.
the AI SDK's wire form of a turn: JSON chunks sent one after another, each with a `type` such as `text-delta`, `data-reply` or `finish`, which the page's `useChat` reads.

a pod's records of one kind, such as medications, as its judgments leave them: one line for each thing however many sources reported it. A named question such as `pod/My medication history` returns a view's rows.
one thing in a view, such as one medication or one lab result: the records that are one thing, shown as one. A row names it in `entry`, by an IRI that ends in `#` and 64 hexadecimal digits.
